title: KV cache warmup smoothing — incident retro & action items
creator: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:
During a capacity rebalancing event on 2026-03-09 we observed a sustained p95/p99 latency increase for text-generation requests on a subset of customer traffic (INC-5879). The immediate symptom was an elevated token latency spike for ~12 minutes for requests routed to two AZs, causing degraded tail latency and a small increase in error retries.

Impact:
- Affected ~8% of hosted API requests for 12 minutes (temporary spike during autoscaler activity).
- Several customers reported slow responses and one customer ran into a user-visible timeout.
- Internal dashboards showed KV cache hit-rate dropping from 92% to 34% on the affected pool; scheduler batching efficiency dropped ~18%.

What happened (concise):
- Autoscaler decision to drain and reprovision a portion of the Dedicated pool coincided with a scheduler rollout that introduced a more aggressive kernel-affinity heuristic (deployed 2026-03-09 02:14 UTC).
- The new heuristic increased path reassignments for requests with long-context indicators, causing many active worker slots to invalidate local KV caches and route a surge of new prefixes to warmed-down workers.
- Because the runtime's KV warmup is conservative, those workers served the first few requests cold; combined with less effective batching (small batch windows) this produced token spikes and increased p99.

Root cause analysis (evidence):
- Timeline correlation between the kernel-affinity heuristic rollout and the latency spike (traces + deploys): see trace timeline in Grafana (link in Links).
- Heap of restart/drain events in the autoscaler logs at 02:18 UTC that caused burst fan-in onto fewer workers (logs attached).
- KV cache heatmap shows eviction and slow refill: cache-hit drop matches tail-latency rise per request ID sampling.
- Scheduler metric "route_reassign_rate" increased 9x immediately after the deploy; post-rollback it dropped back to baseline.

Mitigations performed during incident:
- Rolled back the kernel-affinity heuristic at 02:26 UTC (partial rollback + full rollback by 02:34 UTC).
- Temporarily disabled aggressive drain in autoscaler for the affected pool to prevent repeated fan-in.
- Increased short-term request retry budget for the customer path to absorb a few client timeouts.

Why this wasn't caught earlier:
- Canary traffic did not surface the problem because the warmup workload distribution in canary tests missed the long-context prefix distribution present in production traffic for those customers.
- Our regression harness exercises kernel selection correctness and steady-state latency but doesn't simulate autoscaler-induced mass reassignments with cold KV state.

Action items (see list below for owners/dates):
- Short-term runtime changes to smooth cache warming and reduce cold-first-request penalty.
- Scheduler rollout controls: add deployment gating and a soft-backoff for path reassignment rate.
- Autoscaler policy change: add a drain throttle when reassign rate exceeds threshold.
- Add new regression test that simulates warm->cold worker fan-in and measures p95/p99 impact.

Notes and links to artifacts (internal):
- Incident ticket: INC-5879
- Dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/runtime/kv-warmup-playback
- Traces: https://jaeger.redwood.ai/trace?query=INC-5879
- Confluence retro: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/KV+Warmup+Smoothing+Retro
- PR with temporary rollback: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4217
- Proposed warmup smoothing PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4225

2026-03-11 09:30 - Engineering triage: Rafael confirmed kernel-affinity heuristic as primary correlation; assigned follow-ups and owners.
2026-03-12 15:05 - Rafael pushed prototype for cache warmup smoothing (PR 4225), internal perf runs show p95 improvement in synthetic fan-in test.
2026-03-13 11:48 - PM review complete; added acceptance criteria for the regression test and rollout gating.
action_items: Implement 'warmup smoothing' in KV cache: exponential backoff on eviction + aggressive prefetch of top prefixes (owner: Rafael Ortiz, due: 2026-03-20, ticket: ENG-75124)
Add a 'reassign-rate' circuit-breaker in scheduler: when path_reassign_rate > 3x baseline, suspend aggressive affinity changes (owner: Priya Natarajan, due: 2026-03-18, ticket: ENG-75130)
Autoscaler drain-throttle: limit concurrent drains impacting same logical pool to 2 per 10m (owner: Omar Khalid, due: 2026-03-17, ticket: ENG-75131)
Create a synthetic regression test that reproduces autoscaler fan-in with cold KV state and measures p95/p99 (owner: QA Team, due: 2026-03-22, ticket: ENG-75135)
Canary coverage update: include long-context prefix distributions and autoscaler drain scenarios in the canary workload (owner: DevEx, due: 2026-03-25, ticket: ENG-75136)
Add rollout gating to kernel-affinity flags: require 30m observation window with reassign_rate <= 1.5x before fully enabling (owner: Runtime SRE, due: 2026-03-19, ticket: ENG-75132)
Customer follow-up and RCA note: proactive outreach to affected customers with summary and remediation timeline (owner: CS lead - Elena Park, due: 2026-03-14)
Post-deploy smoke and stress run: execute bench with real-prefix traces for 48h after runtime-1.19 patch (owner: Benchmarking team, due: 2026-03-26)
Document lessons learned in incident playbook and update runbooks for KV cache warmup (owner: Maya Chen, due: 2026-03-21)
Security review for cache prefetch feature (owner: Security - Andre Silva, due: 2026-03-23)
Link and close follow-ups: track completion under project 'runtime-stability' and link back to ENG-74200 parent.
